proof_summary: Pascal’s identity and the adjacent-binomial relation rewrite the summand in the denominator-free form \(T_N(k)=A^2(A+2C)\); setting \(M=np^{r-1}\) and splitting \(k\) into \(pj\) and \(pj+t\), p-adic unit-part product congruences for adjacent binomial coefficients (with valuation-dependent mixed precision) show that every diagonal term \(T_{Mp}(pj)\) matches \(T_M(j)\) modulo \(p^{3r}\). The off-diagonal blocks reduce to \(2(Mp)^2\) times a binomial-cube-weighted inverse-square moment, and recursive grouping into unit blocks of increasing powers of \(p\), together with cancellation of inverse and inverse-square sums, makes this moment vanish modulo \(p^r\), supplying the remaining factor needed for divisibility by \(p^{3r}\).
